key_insight: Exciton transport in perovskite nanocrystal solids is controlled more by energetic disorder than by structural polydispersity, so more uniform particles can still transport excitons worse.
engineering_relevance: Ligand selection is a key design lever for tuning disorder and improving optoelectronic performance in perovskite nanocrystal LEDs, lasers, and solar cells.
method: Resolved exciton dynamics in space, time, and energy
Compared nanocrystal solids synthesized with different alkylamine ligand lengths
Linked transport efficiency to structural vs energetic disorder
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that shorter ligands produce more polydisperse solids, while longer ligands yield more monodisperse but smaller, more quantum-confined nanocrystals with increased energetic disorder and less efficient exciton transport.
watch_item: The conclusion is based on disordered nanocrystal solids in solution-processed films, so device-level performance may also depend on film morphology, interfaces, and stability.
paper_title: Exciton Transport in Disordered Perovskite Nanocrystal Solids
